summary.text: A 55-year-old woman, a poultry farmer with rectal cancer diagnosed and resected at another hospital three months earlier, prior admissions for postoperative intestinal obstruction managed conservatively and prior cholecystectomy, was admitted with a 1-month history of recurrent colicky abdominal pain, bloating, nausea, vomiting and constipation.

After admission hypotension, electrolyte imbalance and fever developed; urgent laparotomy was performed after ineffective conservative management, and she was transferred to the ICU intubated and ventilated, hypotensive on phenylephrine, tachycardic, with coarse breath sounds, a soft tympanitic abdomen and no bowel movements or flatus; WBC 3.43 x10^9/L, neutrophils 79.7%, procalcitonin 65.72 ng/L.

Empiric imipenem-cilastatin plus vancomycin failed (persistent fever, multiple organ dysfunction despite CRRT, fluids, vasoactives, transfusions); regimen changed to meropenem plus vancomycin; blood cultures had no growth and wound secretion culture grew vancomycin-intrinsically-resistant E gallinarum (Group D), mNGS was not available.

Therapy was adjusted to levofloxacin plus meropenem with temperature normalization, de-escalated to levofloxacin and aztreonam, infection markers normalized after 1 week, she was transferred to a specialized department for aztreonam, antibiotics were discontinued, and she was discharged.
